chapter: New Orleans pianists and Clarence Williams
title: Richard M. Jones and Clarence Williams as pianists and publishers
summary: Both wrote many tunes but he judges neither a very good pianist; he recalls Williams's music stores.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: A couple of other fellas that maybe they were, left Chicago, I mean they went up to Chicago and different places before you were grown. Richard M. Jones, Mione Jones, did you ever hear him?
Oh I know it, Mione Jones, before he left here and then when I went to Chicago I met him and we used to be around Clarence Williams when Clarence Williams had the music store. I know it.
Both of those men, they wrote a lot of pieces but were they really first rate pianists? I couldn't tell from the record.
I'll tell you, Mione Jones wasn't a very good piano player and then Clarence Williams wasn't what you call a good piano player.
I didn't think so either from the records.

They wrote a lot of good composers. No, they wrote a lot of good tunes and they had another one that used to be with him, George Jones, he played piano. He wasn't much of a piano player. Well he wrote a couple of tunes with Williams and he was up there with Williams when they had two music stores. They had one at 30 Foison State, one at 47 and they stayed there and finally they went to New York. And Clarence Williams, Foison used to play drum around here, then he started playing piano and he's a comedian. Then he had a show, he opened up a show called The Rosebud up on Dry Snail Phillip.
